key_terms.meaning: A named value fixed with let; it cannot be reassigned after it is set.
A named value declared with var; it can be reassigned while the program runs.
A symbol such as +, == or && that combines or compares values and returns a result.
Statements such as if, guard, switch and loops that choose which code runs next.
A named block of code with parameters and an optional return type that you call by name.
A value type that groups related properties and methods and is copied on assignment.
A reference type that groups properties and methods; two variables can point to the same instance.
A class's ability to take properties and methods from a parent class and add or change them.
A subclass's replacement of a method, property or initializer that it inherited from its parent.
Xcode's software model of an iPhone or iPad that runs an app on the Mac for testing.
A marker in Xcode that pauses the running app at a chosen line so you can inspect state.
A visual file of scenes and connections that Interface Builder edits and the app loads at run time.
The object that owns one screen, loads its view and coordinates user input and data display.
A storyboard connection that gives Swift code a reference to a view object.
A storyboard connection that calls a Swift method when a control fires an event such as a tap.
A UIKit view that shows a scrolling list of rows and asks a data source for each row on demand.
A constraint-based layout system that computes each view's position and size from equations.
A container view that arranges its arranged subviews in a row or column with spacing and alignment.
A container view controller that keeps a stack of screens and shows a navigation bar and back button.
A storyboard-defined transition that pushes, presents or otherwise moves to another view controller.

takeaways: Use let for values that never change and var only for values that do, so the compiler can enforce type safety.
Operators, control flow and functions turn stored values into behaviour, and Swift checks their types at compile time.
Choose a struct for copied value data and a class when identity, shared state or inheritance is needed.
An iOS app moves from source to simulator or device through compile, link, install and launch, and breakpoints pause it for inspection.
UIKit supplies views, a view controller owns a screen, and outlets and actions connect that screen to Swift code.
A table view asks its data source for a row count and reusable cells, so large lists stay fast.
Auto Layout constraints and stack views replace fixed frames, letting one screen fit many sizes and rotations.
A navigation controller manages a stack of screens, and a segue both pushes a screen and carries data forward.
bank_note: Long answers usually test Swift value and reference semantics, the Xcode build-debug loop, and the storyboard-to-code wiring of a table view screen with Auto Layout and a navigation segue.

bank.q: Explain how Swift constants and variables work, why every value has a type, and how type inference differs from an explicit type annotation. Use one example of each.
outline: let declares a constant, var declares a variable
annotation states the type after a colon
reassignment is legal only for var

bank.q: Describe Swift control flow with if, guard, switch and a loop. Give one short example where guard exits early and improves readability.
outline: guard requires a true condition to continue
switch matches patterns and must be exhaustive
loops repeat with for-in or while
guard example unwraps or validates input

bank.q: Compare a Swift struct and a Swift class with respect to assignment, copying, reference sharing and inheritance.
outline: struct is a value type copied on assignment
class is a reference type shared through references
structs can have methods and initializers
mutation rules differ for let instances

bank.q: List the stages Xcode uses to build, install and launch an iOS app on a simulator, and explain what a breakpoint does.
Explain how a storyboard scene, a view controller, an outlet and an action work together when a button tap changes a label.
Write Swift code for a function that takes an array of Int marks and returns the average as Double, using guard for an empty array.
outline: function signature with parameter and return type
sum with a loop or reduce

bank.q: Design a model with a struct Book and a class Library that stores books. Explain where copy behaviour and shared reference behaviour matter.
outline: Book struct with title and author
Library class with an array property

bank.q: Describe how to build a screen with a text field, a button and a label in Interface Builder, including the outlet and action connections.
outline: control-drag outlet for label and text field
control-drag action for button touch up inside
action reads text and updates label

bank.q: Given an array of city names, outline the table view data source methods needed to show one city per row and explain cell reuse.
outline: set cell text label to array row

bank.q: Write the Auto Layout constraints for a label centred horizontally with 16-point leading and trailing margins on any iPhone. Explain why no fixed width is needed.
outline: width follows margins on each screen

bank.q: Describe how a navigation controller pushes a detail screen through a segue and passes one selected item to that screen.
outline: embed list screen in navigation controller

bank.q: A two-screen app shows a list and a detail page. Analyse the flow from the model array to the table view row, through the segue, to the detail outlets and back navigation, naming each object's job.
outline: model array owned by list view controller
table view data source supplies count and cells
prepare passes selected model to detail

bank.q: Evaluate this layout plan: give every view a fixed frame in points. Explain why Auto Layout constraints and stack views are safer across screen sizes and both orientations.
outline: fixed frames fail on other widths
Auto Layout solves equations from constraints

bank.q: A student's table view crashes when it returns a row but the data array is empty. Analyse likely causes and state the checks you would add before returning a cell.
outline: row count and array count must agree
index out of range from stale count
guard index path row < array count

glossary.def: The compiler's ability to deduce a value's type from its initial value without an explicit annotation.
Writing a colon and a type after a name to state the type explicitly.
Writing \(expression) inside a string literal to insert that expression's text.
An if let or guard let construct that unwraps an optional only when it contains a value.
An ordered collection that stores values of one type at integer indices.
An unordered collection that maps unique keys to values.
A block of code that can be passed and called later, like a function without a name.
A value or computed value stored on or provided by a type or instance.
A special method that prepares a new instance by setting its stored properties.
A class that inherits from another class and can add or override behaviour.
The class from which a subclass inherits properties and methods.
A situation where two class instances strongly refer to each other and neither is freed.
One screen's worth of views and a view controller inside a storyboard.
A reusable view that draws one row of a table view.
The object that supplies a table view's row count and cells.
An object that receives callbacks, such as selection or layout events, from another object.
A string that lets a table view recycle a cell of the correct prototype.
The part of a screen not covered by status bars, home indicators or other system UI.
The natural size a view wants based on its content, such as a label's text.
A constraint priority that resists a view growing larger than its intrinsic size.
A constraint priority that resists a view shrinking below its intrinsic size.
The ordered list of view controllers a navigation controller manages, with the last one on screen.
A segue that returns from a scene to an earlier view controller in the storyboard.
A small key-value store for user preferences that persists across launches.
